summary: Mudagamuwe Maithrimurthi is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He held posts at Leipzig University, Heidelberg University, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Muhamad Saputra is a PhD student attested in 2026 at the Australian National University, studying under doctoral supervisor Assa Doron.

Mumon Yamada (1900–1988) was a Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies scholar who studied at Hanazono University and under Seisetsu Seki. He served as abbot of Shofuku-ji (~1949–1988), president of Hanazono University (1949–1978), and head of the Institute for Zen Studies.

Mun-keat Choong is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Paramadhamma Buddhist Institute, Komazawa University (BA), and the University of Queensland (MA and PhD), where Roderick S. Bucknell supervised his MA.

Munenobu Sakurai (born 1961) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his doctoral coursework at Tohoku University (~1986–1989), later serving as assistant professor at Iwate University and professor at Tohoku University (~2005).

Muneo Tokunaga (1945–2016) was an Indologist who studied at Kyoto University and earned his PhD from Harvard University. He taught at Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1982–1988) and Kyoto University as assistant professor (~1988–1990) and professor (~1990–2008).
Muneyoshi Yanagi (1889–1961) was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki (~1904–1910) and at the University of Tokyo (~1910–1913).
Mungunchimeg Batmunkh is a scholar of religious studies and Tibetology who completed a Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna under doctoral supervisor Brigitte Marschall (attested 2010).

Munis D. Faruqui (born 1967) works in Indology and history/archaeology. He has served as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley (~2003) and as Director and Sarah Kailath Chair at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (attested 2026).

Murray Barnson Emeneau (1904–2005) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Dalhousie, Oxford, and Yale under Franklin Edgerton, Edgar Sturtevant, and Edward Sapir. He taught Latin at Yale and served as professor of Sanskrit and linguistics at UC Berkeley (1940–1971).

Musashi Tachikawa (born 1942) is an Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Nagoya University and Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He held posts at Nagoya University, the National Museum of Ethnology, and Aichi Gakuin University.

Muzaffar Alam (born 1947) is a historian and Indologist who studied at Jamia Millia Islamia, Aligarh Muslim University, and Jawaharlal Nehru University. He taught at JNU (~1973–2001) before becoming a professor at the University of Chicago (~2001).

Myles Dillon (1900–1972) was a Celticist and Indologist who studied at University College Dublin and in Europe. He held positions at Trinity College Dublin, UCD, the University of Wisconsin-Madison, the University of Chicago, and the Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies.
Myokyo-ni (1921–2007) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at the University of Graz, as well as under Walter Nowick (~1960–1972) and Soko Morinaga (1984).
Myosei Tatsuguchi (born 1932) is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor (attested 1987) and later professor emeritus (attested 2015) at Ryukoku University.
Myoshin Fujitake is a scholar of Buddhist studies who served as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies at Otani University and as a committee member for the Otani Society (attested 2000).

Mysore Hiriyanna (1871–1950) was an Indologist and philosopher educated at Madras Christian College. He worked at the Oriental Research Institute and Government Normal School before serving as Professor of Sanskrit at Maharaja's College and the University of Mysore (~1917–1927).

Mysore Narasimhachar Srinivas (1916–1999) was a sociologist who studied at Mysore, Mumbai (under G. S. Ghurye), and Oxford. He held posts at Oxford, M.S. University of Baroda, the University of Delhi, and the Institute for Social and Economic Change.
Mónika Kiss is a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies who studied as a PhD student at Eötvös Loránd University under advisor Masanori Yamaji and teachers Robert F. Rhodes and Nozomu Saito.

N. A. Jayawickrama (born 1920) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He served as a professor at the University of Ceylon (~1958–1976) and at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies.
